finding: There is no live range for this job on the site today (live is null), so nothing can be called too wide, too low or too high yet, and this evidence is not yet enough to set one for all four classes. Built totals for one injector fitted (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): truck 2016 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 5.3L about $446-$773 (2.9-3.9 hr); luxury 2016 Cadillac Escalade 6.2L about $420-$771 (2.9-3.9 hr). Economy 2015 Honda Fit and midsize 2023 Honda Accord Hybrid have no parts figure, so no total: labor alone is about $216-$480 for the Fit (1.8-3.0 hr) and $264-$480 for the Accord Hybrid (2.2-3.0 hr). The parts are null for those two because Honda sells their direct-injection injectors only as a set: the Fit set of four lists at $1,640.85-$1,776.31 and the Accord Hybrid kit at $732.42, and no quality aftermarket single injector with a price was loaded for either car. A dealer repair on those cars would therefore be the whole set, roughly $1,860-$2,260 for the Fit and $1,000-$1,210 for the Accord Hybrid at the same labor figures; those are set jobs, not this job's unit, and are given only for scale. All four examples are direct injection, because the only manufacturer bulletins found that print an injector time are for direct-injection engines; no port-injection example was found, and port injectors are usually cheaper and quicker, so this file says nothing reliable about them. How solid the labor times are: all four low ends are manufacturer warranty times for the example vehicle. The GM 2.9 hr (Silverado and Escalade) is the best fit: it is printed for '1-4 injectors on first bank', so it is the time for one injector, on those exact trucks. The Honda times are for the full set: 1.8 hr for all four injectors on the Fit and 2.2 hr for all the injectors plus the affected spark plugs on the Accord Hybrid; neither bulletin prints a one-injector time, and on a direct-injection engine the fuel rail comes off either way, so they are a reasonable stand-in but not a stated one-injector time. The high ends are weak. For the two GM vehicles the 3.9 hr is our sum of GM's 2.9 hr and its maximum 1.0 hr diagnostic add-on, still a warranty allowance and it folds diagnosis in. For the two Hondas the 3.0 hr is the top of a UK vehicle-history site's general '1 and 3 hours', not vehicle-specific. No trade-press or shop book time was found for any of the four vehicles. The luxury parts low end is a discounted genuine GM injector, not an aftermarket one, and the truck's genuine kit (12698484) is the one GM's bulletin names but the catalog page loaded lists it only for 2019-2021 trucks and does not state the quantity in the kit. Against the benchmarks: RepairPal's $768-$953 national average sits at the top of our two built totals, and its parts figure ($464-$507) is three to five times the $98-$149 single GM injector, which suggests it prices more than one injector or dealer-list parts for costlier makes; ConsumerAffairs gives $300 to over $4,000 for a single injector, which shows how wide this job runs. European direct-injection cars (ConsumerAffairs shows $3,112-$3,350 for all injectors on a BMW 740i) are not priced here. Confidence is low: two classes have no usable parts figure, two labor times are for a full set, and no class has a shop-level upper time. Held (2026-11-20, first attempt): no single-injector price for the Fit or the Accord Hybrid (Honda sells sets only), and both Honda times are for the full set. Next attempt: pick economy and midsize examples whose maker sells one injector and prints a one-injector time (GM and Hyundai/Kia four-cylinders are the likeliest).
extras: A quote usually adds diagnosis first (misfire or fuel-trim testing, an injector balance test; GM allows up to 1.0 hr for it and Honda 0.3 hr), and often: new seals, O-rings, clips or a one-time-use fuel pipe where the maker requires them, intake manifold gaskets when the manifold has to come off, an engine oil change if a leaking injector has thinned the oil with fuel, spark plugs fouled by the bad injector, injector coding or a relearn on some engines, shop supplies and sales tax. Shops often recommend replacing the whole bank or the full set at once, and on some cars (the Honda examples here) the maker sells the injectors only as a set, which multiplies the parts cost. Carbon cleaning of the intake valves on direct-injection engines is a separate service.
